text:
maria: Heads-up — after the RBAC refactor (rolehook v3) and last KMS rotation we have a compliance hole: several role grant/revoke events show up in the service traces but are missing from the audit stream. Noticed it while preparing the monthly compliance export.

ken: ugh. which time window? any example event ids?

maria: window 2026-03-19 03:12:00 — 03:17:00 UTC. here's one snippet from the app-side trace (redacted):
```
{
  "ts": "2026-03-19T03:13:21Z",
  "event": "role.modify",
  "role": "data_ingest_writer",
  "target": "service-account:ingest-worker",
  "actor": null,
  "meta": {"path":"/rolehook/v3/apply","refactor":"rbac-v3","kms_key":"K-2026-04"}
}
```

maria: the audit export (s3) has no corresponding `role.modify` record for that ts — the exporter shows a 3-minute gap in role events.

audit-bot: autoparsed alert: audit-export-gap detected for resource_role.events between 2026-03-19T03:11:00Z and 2026-03-19T03:18:00Z. suggested action: gather app logs + kms-proxy logs + audit-proxy logs.

sam: I can grep rolehook-v3 traces in the logging bucket. also, does the audit pipeline depend on actor being present? maybe null actor caused a filter drop.

ken: good call. the audit exporter has a sanity filter that drops events without actor_id to avoid spam. that was added in 2025. during the RBAC refactor we changed who supplies actor mapping (we moved mapping to the KMS-backed credential service). if the KMS key rotated and the credential service failed briefly, actor resolution could've returned null and events got filtered.

leo: if that's true, legal will flag the missing entries for the compliance report. need a timeline and remediation plan.

maria: action plan I propose: 1) sam collect raw logs for the window 2) ken check kms-proxy and credential-service logs for 03:10-03:20 3) export full audit raw stream (pre-filter) from the exporter host if available 4) revert filter to soft-dropping (emit with actor=NULL) until we patch mapping.

ken: I'll look at kms-proxy. quick grep I ran shows repeated `403` errors at 03:12:45 from credential-service->KMS. attaching a short extract:
```
2026-03-19T03:12:44Z credential-service kube: POST /v1/decrypt KMS K-2026-04 -> 403 Forbidden
2026-03-19T03:12:45Z credential-service mapping: actor-resolve failed for token abc... error=kms:access_denied
2026-03-19T03:12:46Z rolehook-v3 apply returned 200 but actor=null
```

sam: grabbing logs now. ETA ~15m.

maria: can we confirm whether the audit exporter kept the raw pre-filter queue? I think we have a backup queue (audit-raw) for 7 days.

audit-bot: audit-raw queue retention: 7d. last successful backup snapshot: 2026-03-19T02:59:00Z. incremental snapshots exist but may be incomplete if exporter crashed during that interval.

maria: ok, that suggests we may not have pre-filter events for the exact window. still need to reconstruct for compliance. if we can show actor resolution failure and KMS 403s, legal might accept a root cause writeup plus mitigations.

leo: also add a note about why actor==null currently results in drop. compliance expects all permission changes recorded. we should not drop; we should emit with actor="UNKNOWN_SERVICE" and include raw token fingerprint.

ken: agreed. I'll prepare an emergency patch to change filter behavior to emit with actor="UNKNOWN" and include a `actor_resolution_error` field. won't try to re-ingest retroactively until we confirm raw messages.

maria: filing an incident ticket now and tagging compliance. ETA for patch?

ken: can cut a PR in 30m, deploy to staging, then hotfix to prod if tests good.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0319-01 severity=P2 assigned_to=ken, incident_channel=#inc-1744001234. please post remediation timeline and list of affected reports.

sam: logs pulled. found 18 role events in app logs with actor=null, all in that 6-min window. uploading artifacts to /mnt/sec-artifacts/INC-2026-0319-01/logs.tar.gz

maria: thanks. next steps: ken -> patch filter and forwarder, sam -> attach timestamps and event ids, leo -> prepare compliance note (impact, root cause, mitigation), me -> update the compliance export story and notify the customer success if any customer-facing reports are impacted.

ken: will also add a smoke test to the exporter to ensure it emits events even when actor resolution fails.

maria: one more ask — check if any role revokes were left unlogged that could cause elevated access. priority: find any `role.grant`/`role.revoke` that affected prod service accounts.

sam: scanning for `prod-` prefixes now. will report back in thread. :mag:

leo: and cc security-compliance@redwood for visibility.

maria: thanks all. I'll keep updates here. :thumbsup:
